title: Ship a scheduled blog collection and a foundry-blog CLI/MCP writer
description:
Foundry sites get a blog whose posts go live on their own: a `blog` page collection whose `publishAt` (UTC ISO) and `draft` are evaluated at REQUEST time (SSR), so a committed post with a future publishAt stays 404 / unlisted until that moment. Writes are git-based through a `foundry-blog` bin (CLI + stdio MCP server) that a producer (Polaris) shells inside the site repo.

Contract: `baseBlogSchema` exported from `@incubrain/foundry/schemas`; nuxt option `foundry.blog: {enabled:false, prefix:'/blog'}`; pages `/blog` + `/blog/<slug>`; `/blog/**` never prerendered; bin `foundry-blog` commands list | get | upsert (JSON stdin) | schedule <slug> --at <iso> | unpublish <slug> | mcp; JSON output `{ok, slug, path, state: draft|scheduled|live, publishAt, commit, pushed}`; refusals `{ok:false, error}` exit 2 (record-dirty, not-a-repo, wrong-branch, invalid, no-post); push only with --push.
Files: layer/content.collections.ts (basePageSchema), layer/modules/rss/, layer/server/mcp/tools/list-pages.ts, layer/package.json (exports ./schemas)
notes: Built on branch feat/blog-publishing (847d4fe, f2bba44; worktree .claude/worktrees/blog), 308/308 vitest, verify + build:foundry green. E2E 2026-10-16 via verdaccio 0.9.0-local.1792175451 in incubrain-website worktree (branch feat/blog: 26f1c54 collection+nav, 5829685 .mcp.json): Polaris publish → live; scheduled → went live at publishAt with no action; withdraw → 404; CLI + MCP list/upsert verified. Remaining (operator): merge + release 0.10.0 to npm, bump website off the -local pin, PR feat/blog → develop. Polish: list date 'Oct 16, 2026' vs post '17 October 2026' (locale/timezone mismatch).

title: Auto UPageHero defaults on: landing pages render a duplicate title banner
description:
## Problem
`basePageSchema` defaults `hero` to `true` (`layer/content.collections.ts:39`: `hero: z.boolean().optional().default(true)`). Since 0.9.0 (product-validator-s5s moved `UPageHero` from the default layout into `layer/app/pages/[...slug].vue`), the auto hero now reliably renders on SSR for **every** content page that omits `hero:` — rendering the frontmatter `title` + `description` as a banner.

Pages that build their own hero via MDC components (landing pages) get a duplicate SEO-title banner above their real hero. It hit astronera.org's live landing page after the 0.9.0 bump ("Dark Sky Conservation Policy for Maharashtra | AstronEra" shown above the hero). Astronera was hotfixed with `hero: false` in `content/pages/index.md` (astronera commit 7c9424c), but every other consuming site is exposed.

Also note: `title` is usually the SEO `<title>` (with a `| Brand` suffix), so it is the wrong string for a visible heading anyway.

## Fix
- Flip the default to opt-in: `hero: z.boolean().optional().default(false)`.
- Add a playground fixture/e2e assertion: a page with no `hero:` key renders NO `UPageHero` in SSR HTML (keep the existing render-hero `hero: true` test).
- Release note in the upgrade guide: sites relying on the implicit hero must add `hero: true`.
- Audit consuming sites (astronera: research.md, team.md currently rely on the implicit default) before release.

## Acceptance
- Content page without `hero:` → no auto hero in SSR HTML.
- `hero: true` → hero renders (existing s5s test still passes).
- Unit + e2e + typecheck green; patch release cut.

title: Foundry sites keep 14 days of Site Events and count visitors without consent
description: From the 2026-09-25 foundry→polaris clarify session. Site Events are pulled by Polaris every 60s from a ring buffer that defaults to the memory driver, so every Railway redeploy/restart loses unpulled rows and Polaris outages cannot be backfilled. This epic makes the buffer durable (Railway Volume + unstorage fs driver, 14-day retention), replaces the persistent localStorage visitor ID with an EU-compliant cookieless daily-salted hash, and adds the Site Events needed for Polaris analytics features 5/8/10 (outbound+downloads, device/browser, 404s). Features 1-4 and 6 (views/uniques, referrer/UTM, goals, entry/exit/bounce, section-depth/duration) already derive from existing rows (ui.page, ui.section, form_submitted, offer_click, page/referrer/utm, visitor.class) — no Foundry work. Probes (uptime, site identity, domain/SSL expiry) live in Polaris, never here: a site cannot observe its own DNS/domain failure. FIELD CONTRACT (Polaris consumes these; update _tools/polaris/docs/log-drain-contract.md): visitor.hash (server-stamped, replaces visitor.anonId); visitor.device ('mobile'|'tablet'|'desktop'), visitor.browser, visitor.os (family names, no versions); name 'ui.outbound' data {host, kind:'outbound'|'download', ext?}; name 'http.not_found' with page+referrer. Paired Polaris epic in _tools/polaris.

title: Generative Engine Optimization: make Foundry sites agent-first
description:
THESIS (operator, 2026-08-31): within 1-2 years most website traffic will be AI agents. Like the desktop->mobile transition, agent-first is the next dominant design target. Foundry must make its sites maximally discoverable, readable, and usable by agents — and must MEASURE the shift (validation layer identity: capture the signal of agent traffic before over-investing).

GROUNDING: two research passes on 2026-08-31 — an external GEO evidence review and a file-level agent-readiness audit of the layer. Key evidence: AI crawlers execute ZERO JavaScript (binary visibility gate); llms.txt is barely fetched by major engines (cheap hygiene only); JSON-LD shows no measured AI-citation lift in 2026 studies (keep @nuxtjs/seo defaults, do not invest further); the best-evidenced content lever is inline citations/stats/named-expert quotes (22-40% citation lift, Princeton/GT); MCP is the one channel where agents ACT, and Foundry already ships list-pages/get-page/what-changed; audit found MCP calls generate zero signal rows and non-JS crawler visits are invisible to the signal stream (client-JS-only page tracking).

TASK ORDER = attack order (lowest effort, highest evidenced return first; deps mark hard gates). EXPLICIT NON-GOALS: no further JSON-LD investment beyond the FAQ/Organization cheap wins; no TLS/network fingerprinting (needs a CDN/WAF Foundry does not have).

title: UPageHero hydration mismatch causes 0.10 CLS on content-driven pages
description:
Default layout's UPageHero v-if reads context.page, which is null when the layout's render function runs during SSR (layout setup completes BEFORE the catch-all page's setup populates context via setContext). Result: SSR emits a v-if comment, client hydration populates context and renders a 448px tall hero, body container shifts from y=84 to y=532. CLS=0.102 on /render-landing, 0.076 on /render-default. Article layout has a related UPageHeader SSR/CSR mismatch (filed separately). App-page versions of the same layouts CLS=0.000.

Root cause: in Vue's slot model, layouts render their own template before the page setup inside <slot/> resolves. Layouts that read page-derived state will always disagree between SSR and CSR.

Fix: move UPageHero out of the layout, into pages/[...slug].vue (above ContentRenderer). Layouts become pure presentation chrome; page-derived UI lives next to the content it describes.
close_reason: UPageHero moved from default layout into pages/[...slug].vue; SSR now emits hero pre-hydration. New e2e regression test (render-hero fixture) + 20/20 e2e, 75/75 unit, typecheck clean. Article-layout UPageHeader variant is NOT the same pattern — needs its own bead.

title: routeRules.appLayout has no effect — layout still resolves to default
description: Setting routeRules: { '/foo': { appLayout: 'article' } } in nuxt.config.ts does not switch the rendered layout. /foo still resolves through the default layout (and 404s because default.vue requires content). Need to either (a) wire a route middleware that reads to.meta.appLayout from the rule and calls setPageLayout(), or (b) rely on Nuxt 4 native support if it exists in 4.4.2 — currently it does not appear to.\n\nAstronera depends on this in nuxt.config.ts:34-50 — if their pages work, it's because they also ship the matching layout files in app/layouts/.
close_reason: Closed

title: Default layout hard-404s any route without a matching content/pages file
description: layer/app/layouts/default.vue:11 throws createError({statusCode:404,fatal:true}) when useContentPage().getPage() returns null. Effect: every app/pages/*.vue that doesn't have a sibling content/pages/*.md returns 404 unless it sets definePageMeta({layout:false}). Both incubrain and astronera work around this by setting layout:false on every app page they author — but the bug means the 'default' layout is unusable for app pages and only the catch-all + content can use it.\n\nFix options: (1) only throw 404 when route is matched by the catch-all (check route.matched), or (2) make the 404 throw conditional on a layout prop, or (3) move getPage() into the catch-all page component and let layouts be content-agnostic.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rendering & routing architecture sync
description:
Items that touch *what gets rendered at which URL*. Relevant to our catch-all + route-rules + content-driven setup.

- v5.6.0 landing: make it optional (#1274)
- v5.6.0 layer: handle docs prefix & folder (#1275)

- v5.11.0 layer: ContentTOC default variant 'circuit' (#1360)
- v5.11.0 toc: wider main grid (#1363)

Approach: review each PR diff against our nuxt.config route rules + catch-all routing before adopting. Goal is to preserve our template flexibility.
notes:
Resolution (2026-05-20):

Investigation found upstream's rendering pattern is LESS flexible than ours, not more.

Comparison:
- Ours: catch-all is layout-agnostic; layout fetches data via useContentPage(); layout selection via routeRules.appLayout (declarative). Supports 4+ layouts on the same catch-all.
- Upstream: catch-all locked to a single layout via definePageMeta({layout:'docs'}); page does fetching; only default + docs layouts; filesystem auto-detection of landing/docs prefix.

Dispositions:
- #1274 landing optional → skip (already-equivalent via routeRules)
- #1275 docs prefix & folder → skip (filesystem auto-detect conflicts with our content-first explicit config)
- #1283 root docs prefix fix → skip (we don't have the bug)
- #1263 homepage llms.txt redirect → skip (clashes with landing; nuxt-llms already handles llms.txt)
- #1264 raw markdown redirects → moved to new bd issue (Vercel-only, orthogonal)
- #1338 forward defaultVariants → adopted (added highlight:true to contentNavigation in layer/app/app.config.ts)
- #1298 sub-navigation → moved to .5 investigate
- #1360 ContentTOC circuit → moved to .5 investigate
- #1363 wider TOC grid → moved to .5 investigate
close_reason: Resolved — see final note. Our rendering pattern is more flexible than upstream's; one small variant default adopted, three items moved to .5, one to new sibling issue.

Mount 'signals' to the unstorage fs driver when an env var (e.g. NUXT_SIGNAL_STORE_DIR, pointing at the Railway Volume mount path) is set; keep memory as the fallback for dev/tests. Add time-based retention: rows older than 14 days are pruned (in addition to the capacity cap); raise DEFAULT_SIGNAL_CAPACITY to fit ~14 days (~170k rows, ~60MB). Head/meta must survive restart (already stored in meta). Add a 'store nearly full' log Site Event at ≥90% capacity. Document the env var in layer/modules/events/AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md. Tests: restart persistence with fs driver in a tmp dir, retention pruning, capacity.
close_reason: Persisted signal buffer via unstorage fs driver (NUXT_SIGNAL_STORE_DIR), 14-day retention pruning + raised capacity to 170k, and a quota_low near-capacity warning event. Tests pass.

title: Count visitors with a cookieless daily-salted hash instead of a stored browser ID
description: Decision (operator, 2026-09-25): the persistent localStorage visitor ID (useUserIdentity.ts) is a stored identifier that needs consent under EU ePrivacy Art. 5(3). Replace it with a Plausible-style server-side hash: sha256(daily_salt + site + ip + user_agent), salt rotated daily and deleted, no client storage. Same value for all 10 adopted analytics features (all are same-day: uniques, sessions, bounce, funnels); lost: cross-day returning-visitor recognition, which no adopted feature needs. Hard to reverse because historical rows switch identity scheme at the cutover. Alternatives rejected: keep localStorage ID (consent exposure); CNIL-exempt audience cookie (France-only interpretation).
close_reason: Decided by operator 2026-09-25 in clarify session

title: Audit Foundry's current monitorability and spec the Polaris status-check contract
description: Inventory what a Foundry site already exposes that Polaris could check (routes, sitemap, existing server endpoints, response headers) and spec the minimal contract Polaris needs: health endpoint shape, page-enumeration source (sitemap vs route manifest), what counts as 'page healthy' beyond HTTP 200, and health of signal-capture endpoints. Output: a decision-ready spec on the epic before any build tasks are created.
notes:
AUDIT — current monitorability surface

Confirmed by code + a live vitest run (71 tests, 11 files, all passing on main):

1. Sitemap: @nuxtjs/seo IS in layer/nuxt.config.ts `modules` (line ~31) and IS active —
   `pnpm exec vitest run` logs "[@nuxtjs/sitemap] No dynamic sources detected" at boot,
   confirming nuxt-sitemap (bundled by @nuxtjs/seo) builds /sitemap.xml from the page tree
   with zero extra config. robots.txt ships the same way (nuxt-robots, also bundled).
   Neither is separately configured beyond `seo: { redirectToCanonicalSiteUrl: true }` and
   `linkChecker: {...}` in layer/nuxt.config.ts — both run on Nuxt defaults.

2. Existing server routes (grepped layer/server + layer/modules/*/server):
   - layer/server/api/_foundry/content/{page,surround}.get.ts — content API for agent tools
   - layer/server/mcp/tools/{get-page,list-pages,what-changed}.ts — MCP tool handlers
   - layer/modules/events/server/handlers/{signals-ingest.post,signals-export.get,webhook.post}.ts
   - layer/modules/rss/server/{routes/rss/[collection].ts,handlers/content-feed.ts}
   No existing bare liveness/health route.

3. /api/_signals/export unauthenticated behavior — confirmed directly from
   layer/modules/events/server/utils/signal-export.ts::checkExportAuth:
   - configuredToken empty (NUXT_SIGNAL_EXPORT_TOKEN unset) -> 503 "Signal export is not
     configured" (never open by default)
   - token present but header missing/wrong -> 401 "Unauthorized"
   Covered by playground/test/unit/signal-export.test.ts already.

4. Headers/caching precedent: layer/modules/rss/server/routes/rss/[collection].ts is the
   only place setting explicit headers (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`). No existing
   `no-store` precedent — /api/_health will be the first.

5. Version plumbing: layer/modules/config.ts already reads the layer's own package.json at
   *build/module-setup time* (node:fs readFile, not request time) and writes
   `nuxt.options.appConfig.foundry = { version, url }`. The only current consumer is
   layer/app/components/app/footer/AppFooterBottom.vue, which reads it as
   `appConfig.foundry as { version: string, url: string } | undefined` (untyped — `foundry`
   isn't declared in any app.config.ts, so it needs a cast). useAppConfig() is already used
   from a *server* handler (layer/modules/rss/server/handlers/content-feed.ts), confirming
   appConfig is safely readable from Nitro routes, not just app code. /api/_health reuses
   this existing build-time value via the same cast — no new file read, no new plumbing.

6. siteId plumbing: layer/nuxt.config.ts already declares `runtimeConfig.public.siteId: ''`
   (NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_ID via Nuxt's standard env mapping). signal-buffer.ts::resolveSite()
   reads it via `useRuntimeConfig(event).public.siteId` but falls back to the request host
   when unset — that fallback is right for stamping signal rows but wrong for a health
   identity payload, so /api/_health reads `public.siteId` directly and returns `null` when
   unset (does not call resolveSite).

SPEC — Polaris status-check contract

- `GET /api/_health` — cheap liveness+identity, no auth, no useStorage/content access:
  200 JSON `{ ok: true, service: 'foundry', version: <layer package version>, siteId:
  <NUXT_PUBLIC_SITE_ID or null>, timestamp: <ISO 8601> }`. `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Page enumeration: `GET /sitemap.xml` (already live, zero config needed). Polaris HEADs
  every URL it lists.
- Signal-plumbing check: `GET /api/_signals/export` with no Authorization header — 401 or
  503 both mean "alive, signal pipe reachable"; 404 or 5xx-other or timeout means broken.
  No change needed to signals-export — behavior already matches this contract.

IMPLEMENTATION DECISION — route location
New file: layer/server/api/_health.get.ts (Nitro file-based route -> `/api/_health`),
sibling to the existing layer/server/api/_foundry/* content routes and following the
underscore-prefix convention already used for internal endpoints (_foundry, _signals).
Not placed under a module (events/rss) since it is layer-wide identity, not
signal-specific.
close_reason: Audit complete; spec captured in notes. Sitemap confirmed live via @nuxtjs/seo. Proceeding to implement /api/_health as product-validator-591.2.

title: Ratify the Foundry→Polaris signal transport design
description: Proposed (see session brainstorm, 2026-08-20): PULL model. Polaris is local-first (desktop/Tauri, later mobile) and not publicly addressable, so push-webhooks from public Foundry sites cannot reach it without an always-on relay. Instead: each Foundry site buffers a unified signal stream server-side and exposes an authenticated cursor-based export endpoint (GET /api/_signals/export?since=<cursor>, bearer token minted per-site in Polaris). Polaris server polls on its scheduler, appends per-site JSONL (its existing durable-store discipline), dedupes by event id, mines anomalies locally. Envelope: {id, ts, site, kind: event|log, name|category, severity?, visitor:{anonId, class: human|agent|bot}, page, referrer, utm, data}. Buffer via Nitro unstorage (fs driver on Railway/Docker, KV driver on Vercel, memory in dev), capped ring buffer (~10k rows / 7d). Grafana-class consumers use the same endpoint or a later generic push drain — envelope stays provider-neutral. Confirm or amend before implementation tasks start.

title: Set up verdaccio local-registry workflow for testing layer changes in external consumers
description:
Need a way to test local foundry layer changes against external consumer repos (astronera, incubrain) before publishing to npm. pnpm's link: protocol doesn't work cleanly cross-repo: link target keeps its own dep tree in the source repo, and ESM resolution can't cross pnpm's strict isolation boundary. Verdaccio gives a local npm registry. Workflow: pnpm publish layer to localhost:4873 with @local tag → consumer does pnpm add @incubrain/foundry@local --registry http://localhost:4873 → tarball flows through normal pnpm install with full transitive resolution.

title: @nuxt/content 3.13 SSR query fails under h3@1: event.req.headers.entries is not a function
description:
When the layer's catch-all calls queryCollection('pages').path(...).first() during SSR, the auto-imported client queryCollection performs an HTTP roundtrip via event.$fetch('/__nuxt_content/<collection>/query'). Under our pinned h3@1 + @nuxt/content@3.13, that internal fetch throws 'event.req.headers.entries is not a function' because content expects h3 v2 Web Headers but Nitro on h3@1 still uses Node-style header objects.

This silently swallows the error inside useAsyncData and returns null → catch-all 404s for every content URL during SSR in dev.

Workaround applied: useContentPage.getPage now uses @nuxt/content/server's queryCollection(event, ...) directly when import.meta.server. Bypasses the HTTP layer entirely on server. Real fix is to upgrade h3 to v2, which cascades into unhead@3 + nuxt-seo@5.1.3 — currently blocked by other peer conflicts.

title: Bump nuxt-og-image to v6 to enable ogImage.sitemap option
description:
Upstream docus v5.9.0 #1312 #1324 added 'ogImage: { sitemap: "/sitemap.xml" }' which forces static OG image generation per sitemap URL at build time.

Currently blocked: our active nuxt-og-image is v5.1.13 (via @nuxtjs/seo), which doesn't have the 'sitemap' module option. We also have v6.3.2 in node_modules from another transitive dep but it's not resolved by our layer.

Fix: either (a) pin nuxt-og-image to v6 in layer/package.json, or (b) bump @nuxtjs/seo to a version that bundles nuxt-og-image v6.

Risk: v6 may have other breaking changes. Verify by running build after bump.
notes:
Resolution (2026-05-20):

Attempted: pnpm update @nuxtjs/seo --latest, which bumped 5.1.0 → 5.1.3 and pulled nuxt-og-image v6.5.0 transitively.

Result: cascading peer-dep conflicts. The newer @nuxtjs/seo brings nuxt-seo-utils + nuxt-schema-org versions that depend on unhead@^3, while our other deps stay on unhead@^2. Also pulls h3@2.0.1-rc.11 alongside h3@1.15.11 already in tree, producing extensive H3Event type incompatibilities in our rss, mcp, and middleware modules.

Conclusion: this is a coordinated dep-bump task (unhead 2→3 + h3 1→2), not a single-package upgrade. Blocked behind that work.

Reverted layer/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml; playground build still passes.
